text: Hey everyone, today we are diving into SageMaker pipelines AWS solution for automating end-to-end machine learning workflows. If you are manually running training scripts, swapping data between S3 buckets and trying to keep track of which model version had which metrices, this video is for you. We are going to build a production grade ML pipeline that handles everything from data prep-processing to model training to model registration completely automated. Let's jump in. So what exactly is a SageMaker pipeline? Think of it as a DAC or directed asyclic graph where each step in your ML workflow is a node and SageMaker automatically handles the execution data flow and dependencies

Between them. Our pipeline has three main steps. Pre-process data, train model, and model registration. The beauty here is that SageMaker handles all the compute provisioning, data passing between the steps and tracks everything. No more manual coordination. Let's dive into the code. First, the pre-processing. We are using a script processor that runs a pre-process. py script on a managed compute instance. This is how our pre-process py looks like. Now notice that how we define the processing inputs. We are pulling our raw train test and validation park files from S3. The processor runs our script and then processing outputs automatically saves the process data back to S3 in the data

Folder. The key thing here is that we are not hard- coding anything. Everything comes from our pipeline config file. This means changing data sets or instance types is as simple as updating one config file. Infrastructure as code at its best. Next, the training step. We are using Sage Maker's hugging face estimator which comes preconfigured with PyTorch and Transformers. This is how our train py looks like. Also we are using step prep-process.properties to dynamically reference the outputs from the previous prep-processing step. This creates a dependency change. Sage maker knows it can start training until pre-processing completes and if pre-processing fails the whole pipeline stop. No wasted compute, no partial

Runs. The estimator automatically provisions a GPU instance in our case which is a G4 instance. It runs the training and saves the model artifacts to S3 bucket all logged and tracked. Finally, model registration. This is a huge for production ML. We are using register model to push our train model into SageMaker's model registry. A few critical thing happen here. First, we automatically attach the model matrices. This means that every registered model has its own performance metrices F1 score, precision, recall permanently attached to it. Second, the approval status is set to pending manual approval. This is basically a governance gate. Before this model can be deployed,

Someone needs to review those matrices and explicitly approve it. And third, we are specifying which instance type this model can run on for inference. This prevents someone from accidentally deploying a model on an instance that's too small or too expensive. All of this metadata makes the model registry a single source of truth for model versions, performance, and deployment history. Now, let's bring it all together. These three steps get packed into a pipeline object. When we call pipeline.absert, Absurd SageMaker creates or updates the pipeline definition in the account. Then pipeline.st start kicks off an execution and this is completely serverless. SageMaker handles the scaling, retries, logging and

Everything. Let me show you what this looks like in a SageMaker Studio. Here you can see all three steps, their status, execution time and you can click into any step to see logs, inputs, outputs and matrices. You can also see our model now sitting in the model registry with all its metadata. And that's SageMaker pipelines. We went from manual script execution to a fully automated ML workflow. This same pattern works for any ML use case. computer vision, NLP, time series forecasting or anything that you can name it. Thank you for watching.
